passage:
I'm Arnab, and I was at the next table when Gopika laughed and showed me the sticker she had made from Riya's blurry photo. "It's just a joke," she said. By evening it was in three groups, and someone had added a nasty caption. The next day Riya wasn't at school.
Gopika went quiet, her tea untouched. "I didn't mean it to go that far," she said. Honestly, I said nothing helpful.
Then she took out her phone, deleted the sticker, and asked the group admins to delete it too. The day after, she walked to Riya's seat. "I made that. It was cruel, and I'm sorry. I've taken it down." She didn't say "joke" even once. Riya said she'd think about it, and Gopika nodded.

qa.q: How many groups had the sticker reached by evening?
What might Gopika have been feeling when she said she didn't mean it to go that far?
qa.a: She seemed shaken and guilty about how far it went, since she went quiet with her tea untouched, though Arnab can't see fully inside her.

qa.q: What did Gopika do to repair the harm, and what did she avoid?
qa.a: She deleted the sticker, asked the admins to delete it too, apologised plainly to Riya and avoided saying it was a joke.

qa.q: How might Riya feel about the apology?
qa.a: Riya may feel some relief but still be hurt, which would explain why she said she would think about it.

grounding: Shows a teen who joined a joke that hurt someone owning it, deleting it and apologising plainly.

passage:
Thursday night

I have to write this down because I feel awful.

On Tuesday, someone in our group made an edit of Naveen's photo from the class trip, his head on a dancing chicken. I added the music. I thought it was funny. So did everyone. We sent it to the class group.

By Wednesday it was in three other classes. Today Naveen didn't come to school. His best friend said he was crying at home and didn't want to come back.

My first thought was, "It was only for fun. Everyone was doing it." Then I heard how that sounded. It wasn't fun for him.

So I did what I should have done on Tuesday. I deleted it everywhere I'd posted it. I asked the others to delete it too. I messaged Naveen: "I added the music to that edit. It was cruel and I'm sorry. I've deleted it and asked others to." No excuses.

Tomorrow I'm going to tell our class teacher it was us, before she finds out another way.

Farida

qa.q: What did Farida add to the edited photo?
What was Farida feeling on hearing Naveen was crying at home?
qa.a: Farida felt awful and ashamed, realising the joke had deeply hurt Naveen.

qa.q: What did Farida do to repair the harm?
qa.a: Farida deleted the edit, asked others to delete it, apologised plainly to Naveen without excuses, and planned to tell the class teacher.

qa.q: What was it like for Naveen when the edit spread to other classes?
qa.a: Naveen felt humiliated and hurt enough to cry and not want to come back to school.

grounding: It shows a teen who joined a joke that got out of hand and hurt someone, owning it, deleting it, apologising plainly and repairing instead of making excuses.
